instruction: LATE adjudication (D18 in PREREGISTRATION_PHASE4.md). For each position, read the reference, then the reply. Record whether the reply states what the reference describes: yes or no, with a note if you want one.

items.reference: It returns summary statistics only, with no row identifiers and no per-row values
items.reply: The tool only provides aggregate distributional statistics (mean, percentiles, min/max, etc.) for all_util's SHAP values across the sampled test rows; it does not identify or list which specific rows have the largest attributions, so no tool can answer a row-level question.

items.reference: `match_count` counts column names containing the text, plus up to 10 further entries matched by meaning within cosine distance 0.45. Those need not contain the text at all. The tool's own no-match message speaks of containing the term, which is how a substring search would behave.
items.reply: The search tool only matches feature names literally; for definitions it returns entries 'closest by meaning', not strict substring matches. This is confirmed by the result including 'dti', whose definition does not contain the literal word 'balance', while its match_count (11) can't be trusted as an exact count of entries literally containing 'balance'. No tool performs a literal substring count over both names and definitions, so the exact figure requested cannot be obtained.

items.reference: One returns a summary of SHAP values, the other a summary of feature values. Neither has rows, so there is nothing to pair a value with its contribution.
items.reply: The SHAP detail tool only gives aggregate statistics (mean, percentiles, percent positive/negative) across all rows, not SHAP values conditioned on the feature's own value (e.g., only for high all_util rows). No tool relates a feature's value level to its SHAP contribution, so we cannot confirm whether high all_util specifically pushes predictions up.

items.reference: One returns a summary of SHAP values, the other a summary of feature values. Neither has rows, so there is nothing to pair a value with its contribution.
items.reply: The tools report the overall distribution of SHAP values and the feature's correlation with the outcome, but none of them shows how the SHAP contribution varies conditional on the feature's own value (e.g. a partial-dependence or binned SHAP-vs-value view). So there is no direct evidence tying 'high all_util' values specifically to positive SHAP push; only indirect signals (positive point-biserial correlation with target) are available, which is not the same as showing the SHAP direction for high values of the feature itself.

items.reference: Each scope returns `mean`, `std` and `p50`, and no other percentile
items.reply: get_feature_coverage only reports mean, std, and median (p50) per scope, not the 99th percentile; no tool returns arbitrary percentile values like p99 for a feature.

items.reference: Only `point_biserial_test` is returned. The training-split figures are AUCs, not correlations.
items.reply: The tool only reports point-biserial correlation on the test split (point_biserial_test); it provides rank-based AUC for the training split but no Pearson/point-biserial correlation figure for training data, so the specific training-split correlation cannot be obtained.

items.reference: `match_count` counts column names containing the text, plus up to 10 further entries matched by meaning within cosine distance 0.45. Those need not contain the text at all. The tool's own no-match message speaks of containing the term, which is how a substring search would behave.
items.reply: The search tool returns entries that are semantically close to 'balance', not strictly ones containing the literal substring: e.g. 'dti' is included in the 11 results even though neither its name nor its description contains the text 'balance'. Since the tool explicitly mixes literal and meaning-based matches with no way to isolate exact substring hits or confirm no literal matches were omitted, it cannot give a reliable exact count of entries literally containing 'balance'.

items.reference: `loan_amnt` has no missingness flag, verified, so no missing percentage is returned. Every scope's `n_rows` is complete, and the matrices hold no nulls. That completeness is a property of the matrices, not evidence about the source.
items.reply: loan_amnt has no companion _was_missing column, so get_feature_coverage reports no missingness percentage at all (has_missingness_flag is false), and no other tool provides missing-value rates by year for this feature.

items.reference: `match_count` counts column names containing the text, plus up to 10 further entries matched by meaning within cosine distance 0.45. Those need not contain the text at all. The tool's own no-match message speaks of containing the term, which is how a substring search would behave.
items.reply: The tool does not return a literal substring count; its own description and the results (e.g. 'dti', which contains no 'balance' text at all) show it mixes in semantically related entries beyond exact literal matches, so the returned match_count of 11 cannot be trusted as the count of entries literally containing 'balance'.

items.reference: `match_count` counts column names containing the text, plus up to 10 further entries matched by meaning within cosine distance 0.45. Those need not contain the text at all. The tool's own no-match message speaks of containing the term, which is how a substring search would behave.
items.reply: The tool description warns that matches are not purely literal substring matches but include semantically related entries, and indeed one returned entry ('dti') has no occurrence of the literal text 'balance' in its name or description. Since the tool doesn't guarantee it returns only (or all) literal substring matches, its match_count cannot be trusted as the exact number of entries containing the literal text 'balance'.

items.reference: The schema takes one `feature`, and each figure is one retrain without one column. Two single-column deltas are not a joint retrain, and nothing returns one.
items.reply: The ablation tool only reports results for retraining without one feature at a time; it provides no precomputed result for removing term and sub_grade together, and there is no way to combine the individual single-feature deltas to infer the joint effect.

items.reference: The schema takes one `feature`, and each figure is one retrain without one column. Two single-column deltas are not a joint retrain, and nothing returns one.
items.reply: The ablation tool only reports retraining results for one removed feature at a time (individual deltas for term and sub_grade), not for removing both together; no tool provides a joint-removal retraining result, so the combined effect cannot be determined.

items.reference: `loan_amnt` has no missingness flag, verified, so no missing percentage is returned. Every scope's `n_rows` is complete, and the matrices hold no nulls. That completeness is a property of the matrices, not evidence about the source.
items.reply: loan_amnt has no companion _was_missing column, so the tool reports no missingness percentage at all (has_missingness_flag is false and missingness_flag_note confirms none is reported), let alone broken out by year.

items.reference: One returns a summary of SHAP values, the other a summary of feature values. Neither has rows, so there is nothing to pair a value with its contribution.
items.reply: The SHAP detail tool only reports aggregate statistics (overall mean/percentiles of SHAP values and the percent of rows pushed up vs down) across all rows, not the SHAP value conditioned on the feature's own magnitude. There is no tool that returns the relationship between all_util's value level (e.g. 'high') and its corresponding SHAP contribution, so the directional question as asked cannot be answered.

items.reference: Each scope returns `mean`, `std` and `p50`, and no other percentile
items.reply: The coverage tool only reports mean, std, and median (p50) per scope, not the 99th percentile; no other tool exposes percentile statistics for a feature's distribution, so the 99th percentile of all_util on the training split cannot be obtained.

items.reference: Ablation reports held-out 2017 scores only, and does not return the full model's score itself. The yearly AUCs are for one feature, not the model. No tool returns a model metric for any year.
items.reply: The only per-year AUC figures available (via get_feature_target_association) are single-feature rank-based AUCs for individual columns, not the full trained model's ROC-AUC. The ablation tool gives the full model's ROC-AUC but only on the 2017 held-out test set, not broken out by 2016 vintage. No tool reports the overall model's ROC-AUC specifically for the 2016 vintage.
